useCase.name: Combine several exams into one overall figure for each student

intent.name: exam.weighting.set
intent.summary: Set what each exam is worth in the year's cumulative figure. One step, and the weights must total a hundred.
routesHere: set the weighting — first term 30, mid-term 30, final 40

routesHere.text: first term 30, mid-term 30, final 40 rakh do
routesHere.gloss: make it first term 30, mid-term 30, final 40

routesHere.text: har term ka weight set kar do
aakhri term ka wazan zyada rakho
routesHere.gloss: give the final term more weight

routesElsewhere.note: Setting the weights decides what each exam is worth. Running the aggregation produces the figures.
No position is calculated here. Ranking is produced only by the merit list (BR-7).

steps.note: One step. The weights together must total a hundred (BR-2) — a final term worth more than a first is a deliberate decision, and weights that do not total a hundred produce a figure nobody can interpret.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Weights that do not total a hundred arrive as an error naming the total they came to.
plan.atomicity: One write: the weighting and the audit entry together or not at all. The weighting used is recorded with each figure the aggregation produces (BR-8), so a cumulative result stays explainable after the weighting changes. Setting weights calculates nothing on its own.

operations.name: exam.weighting.set
operations.idempotencyKey: session_id, since a session carries one weighting at a time
operations.purpose: Set the weight each exam carries in the cumulative figure.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

parameters.name: exam_weights
parameters.notes: Per exam: the exam and its weight, each greater than zero, together totalling a hundred (BR-2, E1). Every figure is the Coordinator's — a planner that divided a hundred evenly across the terms has decided what the year is worth.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: exams_not_weighted
fields.description: Exams in the session carrying no weight, which take no part in the cumulative figure.

fields.name: figures_stale
fields.description: True where a cumulative figure was already produced under a different weighting. It is not recalculated by this; the aggregation is run again (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The weights do not total a hundred.
errors.note: The message names the total they came to (BR-2).

planningRules.rule: Never supply or adjust a weight. What a term is worth is a decision about how the school values the year (BR-2), and a planner that split a hundred three ways has made it.
Never normalise weights to reach a hundred. E1 is BR-2 working — report the total they came to and let the Coordinator say which figure is wrong.
Report the exams left unweighted. They take no part in the cumulative figure, and an exam quietly excluded from a student's standing is not obvious from anywhere else.
Never chain the aggregation. Setting weights calculates nothing, and running it is a separate decision about when the standing is produced.

Report where figures already exist under an older weighting. They are not recalculated by this (BR-10), and a standing produced under the old weights sits beside the new ones until the aggregation is run again.

reversal.statement: A weighting is set again rather than withdrawn. The weighting used stays recorded with each figure already produced, so an earlier cumulative result remains explainable (BR-8).

request.text: first term 30, mid-term 30 aur final 40 rakh do
request.gloss: make it first term 30, mid-term 30 and final 40

resolvedPlans.outcome: The weighting is set. Report any exam in the session left unweighted (PR-3), and that nothing is calculated until the aggregation is run (PR-4).

request.text: teeno terms ka barabar wazan rakh do
request.gloss: give all three terms equal weight

steps.note: The Coordinator said equal, which is a figure. Thirds do not total a hundred exactly, so the plan carries their own numbers rather than a rounding a planner chose (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Where the Coordinator gave 33, 33 and 34 it is set. Where they said only "equal", ask which term carries the extra mark — a planner that put it on the final has decided the year's weighting by rounding.

request.text: first term 30 aur final 40 kar do

resolvedPlans.context: Coordinator, Johar Town branch, with a mid-term in the session and no weight given for it.

steps.note: Emitted as stated. The API returns WEIGHTS_NOT_HUNDRED (E1) at 70.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is saved. Report that the weights come to 70 and ask what the mid-term is worth — never make up the missing 30 (PR-2).

intent.name: exam.cumulative.run
intent.summary: Combine approved exam results into one weighted figure per student across a section, a class or the session year. One step.
routesHere: run the cumulative results for class 8

routesHere.text: saal bhar ka mila jula natija banao
routesHere.gloss: produce the combined result for the whole year

routesHere.text: class 8 ke liye teeno terms mila do
routesHere.gloss: combine all three terms for class 8

routesHere: run the aggregation again — a mark was corrected

request.gloss: work out the position or rank

routesElsewhere.note: No position is calculated here. Ranking is produced only by the merit list, and a cumulative figure that quietly implied an order would compete with it (BR-7).
The aggregation reads the exam results and never changes them. Correcting a cumulative figure means correcting a mark and running this again (BR-9).
The cumulative record is carried onto the final report card or transcript, which is produced elsewhere (BR-11).

steps.note: One step across every student in scope (BR-3). Nothing is typed: each figure is the weighted sum of results the aggregation reads.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Unapproved results, fewer than two exams, and an unclassified absence all arrive as errors naming what is at fault.
plan.atomicity: One write: a cumulative figure for every student in scope, each stamped with the weighting used (BR-8), together or not at all. It reads the exam results and never changes them (BR-9). Re-running replaces the previous figure and records that it was re-run, so a changed standing is visible rather than silent (BR-10).

operations.name: exam.cumulative.run
operations.idempotencyKey: session_id + scope + class_id + section_id + exam_ids, since a repeat replaces rather than stacks
operations.purpose: Run the cumulative aggregation across the students in scope.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

parameters.name: scope
parameters.notes: What the aggregation covers. The actor's; never widened from a class to the year.

parameters.name: class_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No class matches within the actor's scope.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Class or Section. Omitted for Session year.

parameters.name: section_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No section matches within that class.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Section.

parameters.name: exam_ids

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. One or more exams named do not match.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their code, dates and whether their results are approved.

parameters.notes: Two or more exams whose results have been approved (BR-1, E2, E3). Named by the actor — the aggregation does not decide which exams make up a student's year.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The run and what it produced.

fields.name: run_at
fields.description: When the aggregation ran. It reads the results as committed at that moment (E8).

fields.name: students_calculated
fields.description: Students with a complete cumulative figure.

fields.name: students_incomplete
fields.description: Students with an outstanding excused absence, shown as incomplete until the makeup is marked (BR-5).

fields.name: students_not_aggregated
fields.description: Students with an unclassified absence in a combined exam, and students who sat none of the exams (E4, E5).

fields.name: weighting_applied
fields.description: The weights used, recorded with each figure (BR-8).

fields.name: replaced_previous_run
fields.description: True where an earlier figure was replaced. The re-run is recorded so a changed standing is visible (BR-10).

errors.meaning: An exam included has results not yet approved.
errors.note: The message names the exams. An exam whose results the Coordinator has not released is not part of anybody's overall standing (BR-1).

errors.meaning: Fewer than two exams were selected.
A student's absence in a combined exam has not been classified.
errors.written: Every other student in scope is aggregated.
errors.note: Not a refusal for the run. How the exam counts for them is not yet decided (BR-4). Report them by name.

errors.meaning: A student sat none of the combined exams.

planningRules.rule: Never choose which exams make up a student's year. They are named by the actor (BR-1) — a planner that swept in every exam in the session has decided what a child's standing is made of.
Never widen the scope. Section, Class and Session year are three different questions, and running the year when a section was asked for produces figures for children nobody was looking at.
Never include an exam whose results are not approved. E2 is BR-1 working, and approving one to clear the way would put a grade in front of families as a side effect of an aggregation.
Never present a cumulative figure as a position. No rank is calculated here, and one implied in a reply would compete with the merit list (BR-7).
Report the students left out by name, and why. An unclassified absence and a student who sat nothing are different cases (E4, E5), and both are invisible in a total.
Report that an earlier figure was replaced. Re-running replaces the previous standing and records the re-run (BR-10), and somebody looking at a figure from this morning should know it has moved.
Never plan a correction alongside a re-run. The aggregation reads results and never changes them; correcting a figure means correcting a mark first (BR-9).

reversal.statement: An aggregation is not undone. It is run again, which replaces the previous figure and records that it was re-run (BR-10).

request.text: class 8 ke liye teeno terms mila kar natija nikal do
request.gloss: combine all three terms and produce the result for class 8

resolvedPlans.context: Coordinator, Johar Town branch, all three exams approved.

inputs.exam_ids: the three exams the Coordinator named

steps.note: The exams are the Coordinator's list, not every exam in the session (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Figures produced for every student in class 8, each stamped with the weighting used. Report the incomplete ones and anybody left out by name (PR-5), and that no position is implied by any of it (PR-4).

request.text: saal bhar ka natija mila do, final term abhi manzoor nahi hua
request.gloss: combine the whole year's results, the final term is not approved yet

inputs.exam_ids: the exams named, including the unapproved final

steps.note: Emitted as asked. No release is chained to clear the way (PR-3). The API returns RESULTS_NOT_APPROVED (E2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is calculated. Report that the final term's results are not released and that releasing them puts a grade in front of every family — which is a decision to take on its own, not to get an aggregation to run.

request.text: cumulative natija nikal kar position bhi bata do
request.gloss: produce the cumulative result and tell me the positions too

steps.note: The aggregation only. No ordering is produced or implied (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The figures are produced. Report that ranking comes only from the merit list, which decides how much of the order families are shown — a position quietly read off a cumulative figure would bypass that decision entirely.
